core_obligations: Start from a presentation R_f[x_1, ..., x_n] -> A, write R_f = R[x_0]/(fx_0 - 1), and consider the presentation R[x_0, x_1, ..., x_n, x_{n+1}] -> A_g that extends the given map, sends x_0 to the image of 1/f and x_{n+1} to 1/g (proof lines 21022-21026).

Choose a lift g' in R[x_0, x_1, ..., x_n] of g, and from a presentation of M given by a matrix (h_ij) over R_f[x_1, ..., x_n] choose lifts h'_ij in R[x_0, x_1, ..., x_n] of the entries (proof lines 21027-21034).

Display the resulting presentation with source R[x_0, ..., x_n, x_{n+1}] to the power s + 2t and target to the power t mapping onto the localized module, and identify the defining matrix: a first t by s block of the lifted entries h'_ij, a second t by t block (x_0 f - 1) I_t and a third block (x_{n+1} g' - 1) I_t (proof lines 21035-21044).

Conclude that this is a presentation of the localized module over a finitely generated R-algebra, which is exactly the assertion that the localized module is of finite presentation relative to R (proof lines 21040-21045).
proof_roadmap: Rewrite the base ring R_f as R[x_0]/(f x_0 - 1) and extend the presentation of A by the variable x_0 and by a variable killing 1/g (proof lines 21023-21026).
Lift the element g and the entries of the presentation matrix to the polynomial ring over R (proof lines 21027-21034).
Write down the lifted matrix with its three blocks, two of which encode the two localization relations, and read off that it presents the localized module (proof lines 21035-21045).
difficulty_reason: The lemma concerns a finite type ring map R_f -> A, an element g of A and an A-module M of finite presentation relative to R_f, and asserts that M_g is of finite presentation relative to R, not merely relative to R_f (statement lines 21014-21020). The proof is neither a citation nor a formal manipulation: it rewrites the localization R_f as R[x_0]/(f x_0 - 1), lifts the presentation of A, of the element g and of every matrix entry to the polynomial ring over R, and then exhibits an explicit t by (s + 2t) matrix whose three blocks encode the original relations together with the two localization relations f x_0 - 1 and x_{n+1} g' - 1 (proof lines 21023-21044). The point of the construction is precisely the change of base from R_f to R, so that the same module is seen to be finitely presented over R itself. The counted span is self-contained: it refers to no labelled item of the chapter and cites nothing; the printed text writes M_f where the construction presents M_g, and that slip is preserved verbatim.
